text: NEW P0 found (#6757, fix in progress on fix/datetime-julian-epoch): DateTime fields in DBFs were 702 days off from VFP9 in both directions. date_to_julian/julian_to_date subtracted 702 'to match tests' (bulk test commit 2026-04-18, no VFP evidence), and stored milliseconds were truncated, not rounded. Found by an independent VFP9-written DBF fixture, which a reviewer asked for on the aggregates PR (#6755): Copperfin's own writer and reader agreed with each other, so no existing test could see it. Fix uses the true Julian Day Number, rounds stored ms to the nearest second half-up with day carry (VFP9-probed), and moves 16 fixture constants in 4 tests by +702; new test_dbf_datetime_vfp_compat checks both directions against VFP9 bytes. Please do not add tests that hard-code shifted julian numbers; anything that stores a date in a DateTime must use the real JDN (2415021 = 1900-01-01). Also open: #6755 aggregates (will rebase on this), #6756 Currency VAL, #6758 TRANSFORM currency picture.
